correctness.rationale: In the nonpure cases the surviving pure powers cover the source and its closed image. Ordinary vertex charts retain their two linear coordinate ratios except at the tangent vertex. In that chart the omitted u=y/x is the only missing monomial of the full affine semigroup: v,u²,uv,u³ generate every other monomial for d≥3. Thus R=ℂ+I⊂B=ℂ[u,v], I=(v,u²)B. B is finite birational and B/R has length one, generated by the class of u. A nonzero constant term prevents a member of R from multiplying u into R, so the conductor equals I. The four stated generators are independent modulo the square of the maximal ideal I; the localized normalization is the regular ring at (u,v), so the inclusion and length-one cokernel give depth one for R by the depth lemma. For n≥1, I^n as an R-ideal equals I^n as a B-ideal: any B coefficient can be absorbed into the first factor in a product of n elements of I. For v-exponent j=0,…,n−1, the excluded u-exponents run from 0 to 2(n−j)−1; hence ℓ(B/I^n)=n(n+1), and subtracting one gives the asserted Hilbert–Samuel function at n=q+1, including q=0, and multiplicity two. Completion preserves these data. The length-one normalization quotient also subtracts one from the intrinsic projective Euler characteristic. For the pure omission x^d the lone simple base point is [1:0:0]. On its blowup the sections x^(d−1)y and x^(d−1)z cover the exceptional divisor and pull back their target charts to the ordinary two blowup charts. For the first of these the ratios yield both u=y/x and w=z/y, with all other ratios polynomial in u,w; the second chart is symmetric and y^d,z^d cover away from the base point. L=dH−E gives L²=d²−1 and −K·L=3d−1, hence the stated Riemann–Roch formula. The other cases have degree d², and the exceptional exponent patterns have three and six permutations. The frozen finite checker and recorded output were read only; these analytic arguments establish the unbounded degree and length ranges.

evidence: Maddox–Pandey's Theorem 2.3 supplies normalization for nonpure deletion and gives the pure-case exact membership test: in degree sd, a retained exponent must have total at least s outside the omitted variable. Lemma 2.17 has only the original missing monomial when max(m)<d−1. For max(m)=d−1 and d>2, Lemma 2.18 gives exactly the missing exponents (ds−1,1,0,…,0) for s≥1. These semigroup assertions have no characteristic restriction.

evidence: When there is one graded hole m only, the normalization quotient is killed by the irrelevant ideal and vanishes on Proj. When the missing exponents are (ds−1,1,0), invert x^d and take degree zero: these are all the same affine hole u, and no other holes remain. Inverting y^d or z^d kills the quotient. Thus the actual affine ring is already determined by the published list: ℂ+(v,u²)ℂ[u,v]. Its conductor is the displayed ideal, and its m-adic length follows by counting the omitted monomials of (v,u²)^n and subtracting one.

In the pure case the published degree-s semigroup identifies the ring with the section ring of dH−E on the blowup: its basis consists of sections of degree sd vanishing to order at least s at the point. The ample divisor gives back the blowup on taking Proj, and the polynomial follows by counting or Riemann–Roch.

value.rationale: These are naturally motivated geometric invariants and the exposition usefully distinguishes a singular projective point from the cone vertex. As a new finding, however, it adds only the standard projective interpretation and straightforward exact invariant computations of the already determined rings. The precise local Hilbert–Samuel function is mechanically implied by the known single affine hole, so no standalone unestablished but valuable remainder is validated.
